data.name: Tetrobot and Co.
data.detailed_description:
Tetrobot is the world's most popular and reliable robot, but he's not perfect. That's why I, Maya, have built him a microscopic little brother, Psychobot.

Help me guide Psy through Tetrobot's cogs and circuits: by swallowing blocks of matter and spitting them out, we can repair anything. Learn how pipes, lasers, fans and other electronic devices work, learn how to alter the chemical properties of slime, and collect all the memory blocks that you find on the way.

The owners of damaged Tetrobots all around the world rely on us because we are the only people who can repair their precious robots.

Key Features

  • Pure puzzle gameplay for gamers who like to give their minds a workout.
  • Over 50 levels to play and even more secrets to unlock.
  • Original music composed by Morusque (Knytt Stories, Saira, Blocks That Matter, Exodus)
  • Find out what became of Tetrobot, Alexey, Markus and Maya, 15 years after "Blocks That Matter." 

Steam Features

  • Steam Achievements: An even greater challenge for avid gamers.
  • Steam Cloud: Start a game at home, finish it at work (if you're careful).
  • Steam Workshop: Create your own puzzles and share them in one click (available soon).

reviews.review:
Tetrobot and Co. is a wonderfully inventive puzzle adventure that turns the seemingly ordinary task of repairing a robot into an engaging test of intelligence, creativity, and patience. Developed and published by Swing Swing Submarine, the game emphasizes logical thinking and environmental manipulation rather than combat or fast-paced action. Its colorful presentation and adorable robotic characters create a welcoming first impression, but beneath that charming exterior lies a surprisingly sophisticated collection of mechanical challenges. What makes the experience memorable is its ability to transform simple interactions into complicated puzzles that reward experimentation and careful observation.

The adventure follows Psychobot, a miniature robot designed by Maya to enter malfunctioning Tetrobot units and repair their internal machinery. Players navigate intricate mechanical environments filled with electronic components, obstacles, and interconnected systems. The story continues the universe introduced in Blocks That Matter, providing familiar characters and a lighthearted narrative backdrop. Although storytelling remains secondary to gameplay, the premise gives every puzzle a clear purpose and makes exploring the internal workings of these machines feel surprisingly entertaining.

The defining mechanic involves collecting blocks made from different materials and strategically placing them throughout each environment. Every material possesses properties that influence how it interacts with surrounding machinery. Players must understand these behaviors to overcome obstacles, activate mechanisms, and create pathways through increasingly elaborate chambers. Lasers, pipes, fans, and chemical interactions introduce additional complexity, requiring solutions that combine multiple environmental systems. The controls remain relatively straightforward, allowing the difficulty to emerge naturally from the puzzles rather than demanding complicated button combinations.

Level design is undoubtedly one of the game's greatest accomplishments. With more than fifty carefully constructed stages, the experience gradually introduces new concepts before combining them into increasingly demanding situations. Earlier puzzles encourage experimentation, while later challenges require a thorough understanding of previously established mechanics. The progression generally feels rewarding because successful solutions depend on knowledge acquired through earlier encounters. Particularly satisfying are those moments when an apparently impossible arrangement suddenly becomes understandable after recognizing an overlooked interaction between objects.

However, the difficulty occasionally becomes intimidating. Some puzzles require considerable trial and error, and players may spend extended periods searching for a solution without making meaningful progress. The absence of action-oriented distractions places nearly all attention on problem-solving, which can become mentally exhausting during longer sessions. Nevertheless, overcoming these obstacles delivers genuine satisfaction. Players who appreciate methodical challenges will likely find the demanding nature of the experience more rewarding than frustrating.

Exploration receives additional depth through collectible memory blocks and hidden secrets. These optional objectives encourage players to examine environments carefully and discover alternative ways of manipulating machinery. Collecting everything requires more than simply completing the main puzzles, providing worthwhile incentives for completionists. Steam achievements and community-created Workshop content further extend the experience, offering additional challenges beyond the original campaign.

Visually, the game embraces a charming mechanical aesthetic built around colorful blocks, compact robotic characters, and clean geometric environments. Its presentation prioritizes readability, making interactive objects and important environmental features easy to distinguish. Although the graphics are relatively modest, their consistency complements the thoughtful gameplay. The soundtrack by Morusque adds personality through playful electronic compositions that establish a pleasant atmosphere without distracting from concentration. Together, the visuals and audio create an inviting setting that balances the demanding nature of the puzzles.

The game also benefits from its accessible control philosophy. Movement and block manipulation are uncomplicated, and controller support provides an alternative to keyboard controls. However, its deliberate pacing and emphasis on experimentation mean that it will not appeal equally to everyone. Players seeking elaborate storytelling, intense action, or immediate gratification may find the experience repetitive. Its strongest appeal lies in the satisfaction of understanding interconnected systems and applying that knowledge creatively.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially classified as Unsupported. Despite the game's modest technical requirements and controller-friendly mechanics, this classification means reliable functionality on Valve's handheld should not be assumed. Players intending to enjoy the adventure primarily on Steam Deck should consider this limitation before purchasing.

Ultimately, Tetrobot and Co. succeeds because it understands what makes puzzle games genuinely rewarding. Its carefully balanced mechanics, inventive environmental interactions, and consistently clever level designs create an experience that values understanding over memorization. While its occasional difficulty spikes, limited narrative development, and lack of official Steam Deck support represent notable drawbacks, its strengths considerably outweigh these shortcomings. It is a delightful recommendation for anyone who enjoys challenging their mind through imaginative mechanical puzzles.

A charming and intelligently designed puzzle adventure that combines accessible mechanics with substantial intellectual depth, delivering a satisfying experience for patient players who enjoy creative problem-solving.

Rating: 8/10
